text:
Anya: Heads-up: noticed a 12-18% p95 latency regression on the paged-attn path after the runtime kernel-selection change merged yesterday (hash abc123ef). Starting a quick triage thread here.
Ravi: Can you paste numbers + workload? small/large seq? batch sizes?
Anya: Repro is on llama-13b, seq=1024, batching ~8 (steady-state). From our canary traffic: p50 28ms -> 30ms, p95 45ms -> 52ms, p99 120ms -> 160ms. CPU side stable. GPU kernel time increased for some requests.
Marta: perf-bot ran a microbench earlier. Pasting summary:

```
benchmark: rbench --model llama-13b --seq 1024 --batch 8
baseline (pre-abc123):
  total p95 = 45.2ms
  kernels: flash_attn_forward 18.1ms, kv_cache_lookup 3.2ms, fused_mm 5.6ms
after abc123:
  total p95 = 52.9ms
  kernels: paged_attn_dispatch 24.0ms (+32%), kv_cache_lookup 4.1ms, fused_mm 5.8ms
```

perf-bot: top kernel time delta shows flash->paged dispatch increase.
Anya: nvprof snippet (trimmed):
```
Kernel                           Time (ms)   Calls
flash_attn_forward               18.1        512
paged_attn_dispatch              24.0        512
fused_attn_kernel                6.0         512
```

Ben: Is this happening for cold KV cache only or warm as well?
Anya: Both, but worst for cold prefix cases. Warm KV still slower by ~10% p95.
Ravi: What changed in abc123? IIRC it adjusted the kernel-selection threshold to prefer paged-attn for seq>=512 to avoid flash memory pressure. Maybe the threshold was too low.
Marta: I dug into the selection logic: new heuristic picks paged when (seq_len >= 512 || kv_items>max_kv_for_flash) || (batch_time_estimate > 30ms). The batch_time_estimate calculation seems to be inflated for certain seq distributions, so we fall back to paged even when flash would be better.
Anya: Also noticed KV cache hit ratio dropped for a subset of requests (from 0.87 -> 0.72) due to header-normalization change in the same deploy, which makes more requests look like cold prefix (different cache keys).
infra-bot: deploy 2026-03-16T02:12:43 by @ci-user triggered rollout of abc123ef to canary.
Ben: Two orthogonal suspects: (1) selection heuristic being too aggressive for paged, (2) KV-key churn causing cache coldness and pushing more work into paged path.
Ravi: Can we bisect selection-only? Run a branch with only heuristic reverted (keep header change) to separate effects.
Marta: I ran that locally:

```
# baseline with header-change + heuristic reverted
rbench --model llama-13b --seq 1024 --batch 8 --force-kernel flash
result: p95 46.0ms (close to baseline)
# header-change + heuristic enabled
rbench ... --auto-kernel
result: p95 53.1ms
```

Marta: So heuristic seems primary.
Anya: Good. Proposed immediate mitigations:
- revert the heuristic tweak in canary only (Ravi)
- add a conservative guard: prefer flash if seq<=1024 AND batch_size<=16 (Marta)
- add telemetry tags for kernel selection reasons (Ben)
- investigate KV key normalization rollback as follow-up (Anya)
Ravi: I can cut a canary rollback PR today. Also will add a toggled flag so we can A/B test selection.
Ben: I'll add tracing for selection decisions (why paged chosen: reason code) and emit kv_cache_hit boolean per request to see correlation.
Marta: I'll run a focused microbench sweep across seq lens [256,512,768,1024] and batch sizes [1,4,8,16] with both kernels forced and auto so we can create a small decision matrix. Command I used:

```
for s in 256 512 768 1024; do for b in 1 4 8 16; do rbench --model llama-13b --seq $s --batch $b --repeat 30 --record $s-$b.json; done; done
```

perf-bot: queued 16 jobs on perf cluster, ETA 20m.
Anya: Also capture GPU sm_ util and L2 read/write during runs; earlier traces show paged path increased L2 traffic by ~18% which explains some delta.
Ravi: Action items:
- Ravi: push rollback canary + flag (ETA 2h)
- Ben: add selection reason tag and kv_cache boolean to traces (ETA 4h)
- Marta: complete microbench matrix and upload artifacts (ETA 6h)
- Anya: investigate header normalization KV churn and prepare rollback proposal if needed (ETA EOD)

Marta: One more note: fused_attn_kernel was unaffected and still micro-optimised; the regression only hits the dispatch/dispatch-overhead on paged path. Might be an opportunity to optimize paged dispatch or implement a cheaper fast-path for common seq/batch combos.
Anya: Agreed. If rollback reduces p95 back to baseline, we'll keep heuristic change behind a flag and revisit algorithm with empirical matrix.
Ben: I'll also add a short-term config override on Dedicated pools so enterprise customers can pin to flash selection if they see regression.
Ravi: I'll post PR links here when ready.
Anya: Thanks all — keep updates in this thread. If anyone finds a cheap patch to reduce paged dispatch overhead, ping me.

infra-bot: canary rollback started by Ravi at 1965432460
Anya: rollback looks good in canary so far: p95 dropped from 53 -> 46ms in initial 5m. Will monitor and follow up.
